lesson.title: Ratio
lesson.module: Unit 2 Ratio, proportion, Direct Variation and Inverse Variation (Algebra)

items.quote: What you'll learn Ratio. Properties of ratio.
items.text: What you'll learn: Ratio. Properties of ratio.

items.quote: The two terms of the ratio.
items.term: The two terms of the ratio

items.quote: We have learned in the previous phases the subject of ratio
items.text: We have learned in previous phases the subject of ratio, and that ratio is a comparison between two quantities.

items.quote: for example: If there are 4 boys and 3 girls
items.text: For example: if there are 4 boys and 3 girls, the ratio between the number of boys to the number of girls can be written as 4 to 3 or $\frac{4}{3}$. Generally, if a and b are two real numbers

items.caption: Picture of a group of cheering children (boys and girls), illustrating the 4 boys and 3 girls example.
items.notes: Illustrative picture; count of children not verified.

items.quote: the ratio between the two numbers a and b can be written as a to b or a:b or
items.claim: The ratio between two numbers a and b can be written as a to b, or a:b, or a/b.

items.quote: a will be called an antecedant and b is consequent
items.claim: In the ratio a:b, a is called the antecedent and b the consequent; a and b together are the two terms of the ratio.

items.quote: Is the ratio changed if each of its two terms is multiplied
items.text: Is the ratio changed if each of its two terms is multiplied in a fixed amount not equalling to zero? Complete: $\frac{3}{5} \overset{?}{=} \frac{3\times\ldots}{5\times\ldots}$
items.notes: Blanks to fill; '?' above the equals sign.

items.quote: Is the ratio changed if you add a real number to each
items.text: Is the ratio changed if you add a real number to each of its two terms? Complete: $\frac{2}{3} \overset{?}{=} \frac{2+\ldots}{3+\ldots}$

items.quote: If a/b = 3/5, Is a = 3, b = 5 for the values of a and b?
items.text: If $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{3}{5}$, is $a=3$, $b=5$ for the values of a and b?

items.quote: Find the number which if added to the two terms of ratio 7 : 11 it will be 2 : 3
items.stem: Find the number which if added to the two terms of ratio $7 : 11$ it will be $2 : 3$

items.quote: Find the positive number which if we add its square to each of the two terms of ratio 5 : 11 it becomes 3 : 5.
items.text: Find the positive number which if we add its square to each of the two terms of ratio $5 : 11$ it becomes $3 : 5$.

items.text: For More Exercises, go to MOE website

learning_objectives.label: Ratio notation and terms
learning_objectives.description: Write the ratio between two numbers a and b as a to b, a:b or a/b, and name its antecedent, consequent and two terms.

learning_objectives.label: Properties of ratio
learning_objectives.description: Apply the properties of ratio: decide whether a ratio is changed when both terms are multiplied by a fixed non-zero amount or have a real number added to them.
